shortDescription: Module to manage permissions of users/groups in oVirt/RHV

options.name: auth
options.description: Dictionary with values needed to create HTTP/HTTPS connection to oVirt:

options.name: fetch_nested
options.description: If I(True) the module will fetch additional data from the API. It will fetch IDs of the VMs disks, snapshots, etc. User can configure to fetch other attributes of the nested entities by specifying C(nested_attributes).

options.name: group_name
options.description: Name of the group to manage. Note that if group does not exist in the system this module will fail, you should ensure the group exists by using M(ovirt.ovirt.ovirt_groups) module.

options.name: namespace
options.description: Namespace of the authorization provider, where user/group resides.

options.name: nested_attributes
options.description: Specifies list of the attributes which should be fetched from the API. This parameter apply only when C(fetch_nested) is I(true).

options.name: object_id
options.description: ID of the object where the permissions should be managed.

options.name: object_name
options.description: Name of the object where the permissions should be managed.

options.name: object_type
options.description: The object where the permissions should be managed.

options.name: poll_interval
options.description: Number of the seconds the module waits until another poll request on entity status is sent.

options.name: quota_name
options.description: Name of the quota to assign permission. Works only with C(object_type) I(data_center).

options.name: role
options.description: Name of the role to be assigned to user/group on specific object.

options.name: timeout
options.description: The amount of time in seconds the module should wait for the instance to get into desired state.

options.name: user_name
options.description: Username of the user to manage. In most LDAPs it's I(uid) of the user, but in Active Directory you must specify I(UPN) of the user. Note that if user does not exist in the system this module will fail, you should ensure the user exists by using M(ovirt.ovirt.ovirt_users) module.

options.name: wait
options.description: C(yes) if the module should wait for the entity to get into desired state.
